messages.author: 83e4604c4f9feab5
messages.subject: Got some problems with hBayesDM installation
parts:
I'm a psychology graduate student in China.The hBayesDM worked well last year in R 3.5.0,and i employed it in analyzing Iowa gambling task.
Recently i noticed that the new version added a new model，so i updated the package and installed the R 3.5.1.Here comes the tragedy,after installing the package as https://rpubs.com/CCSL/hBayesDM said,the package doesn't work properly.I snapshot the error as a pic in attachment.And i'm a windows 10 user. I've tried to uninstall and reinstall and it's not work.I guess there is something wrong with other dependent packages but i really not sure,so I've to ask for help.
I've tired the igt_pvl and the igt_orl,and got the same error.

B <- igt_pvl_delta(data = "D:/matlab/B.txt", niter = 3000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 3, ncore = 3,adapt_delta = 0.95, stepsize = 1,max_treedepth = 10)
Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) : 
  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! Error in .shlib_internal(commandArgs(TRUE)) : 
  C++14 standard requested but CXX14 is not defined
Calls: <Anonymous> -> .shlib_internal
停止执行
In addition: Warning message:
In system(cmd, intern = !verbose) :
  running command 'C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-35~1.1/bin/x64/R CMD SHLIB file763476f5581c.cpp 2> file763476f5581c.cpp.err.txt' had status 1

Hoping for reply.Thanks.

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Got some problems with hBayesDM installation
parts:
Hi,

I think it's likely an RStan installation problem. We've updated README.md and add a bit more about RStan installation in its GitHub repo (https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM) but not in the rpubs (https://rpubs.com/CCSL/hBayesDM)... I will update the online rpubs tutorial when we release the next version. Please make sure to check if RStan is properly installed first and follow instructions released recently from Stan carefully (https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started). Seb's suggestion is one of them. Please let us know if you continue to have the problem. 

Best,
Young
